attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense) as per-segment DHCP routers so node3 and node4 each obtain addressing (and default route) from the router directly in front of them, rather than static config. node1 hands out 10.50.10.100-200/24 on lan-a with itself (10.50.10.254) as default-router; node3 leased 10.50.10.100 and pings the router. node2 hands out 10.50.20.100-200/24 on lan-b (new opt1 interface on vtnet2) with itself (10.50.20.254) as default-router; node4 leased 10.50.20.105 and pings the router. All 4 nodes were restarted one at a time (with quorum/independent paths preserved) and proven to boot with a new boot identity while recovering full service state and DHCP addressing.
